# A package is one declaration set however many files it is written in, so a
# type annotated in one file may name a type declared in a sibling.
#
# An imported package used to be checked a file at a time -- one Check per
# document, the results merged afterwards -- so each file resolved without its
# siblings in scope. Annotation positions failed on a name the package plainly
# declares; a body reference worked, because those resolve lazily, which is
# what made it look like a type-resolution bug rather than a scoping one.

sngl check app
stdout 'ok'

-- app/main.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import s "../sub"

component main node {
    text(value=string(s.dist(s.origin())))
}

window {
    main
}
-- sub/a.sngl --
import ui "sngl:ui"

struct Pt {
    x int = 0
    y int = 0
}

ui.window {
}
-- sub/b.sngl --
// Every one of these names Pt from a.sngl: a struct field's type, a
// parameter's type, and a body expression.
import ui "sngl:ui"

struct Line {
    from Pt
}

func dist(a Pt) => a.x

func origin() => Pt{x = 0, y = 0}

ui.window {
}
